paragraphs: The CLS 350 has been a key part of the CLS range since the model's inception in 2004. The first-generation C219 (2004–2010) uses the M272 — a 3.5-litre naturally aspirated petrol V6. From 2010, the C218-generation CLS 350 switched to the OM642, a 3.0-litre V6 diesel. This is a completely different engine, not an evolution of the M272. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting. The CLS was discontinued entirely after the C257 in 2023, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLS 350 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the CLS 350 from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLS 350 spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M272 part will work on an OM642 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (M272 or OM642) via registration or VIN - Your generation (C219 or C218) - Drivetrain and ancillary specification - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build
